$comment: Extraction contract AND measurement map. `exportedSelectors` is the ALLOWLIST: extract-maquette-css.py exports only what is listed here. `regions` is what parity-probe.py measures; each region names the states it is visible in. `states` are the ids accepted by window.__go().

chassis/topbar.$note: Direction of truth is INVERTED: the app is authoritative for the shell, the prototype for the pages. Measured against the shipped TopBar.

fiche/non-possede.$note: A suggestion is NOT in the library: the block says « non », shows the follow state, and offers to add — never to delete. Same template, with the only variation reality imposes.

chassis/tiroir.$note: The full template: three titled sections as in nav.ts, the same badges as the bottom bar, and the VersionCard in the footer — the drawer is the only path through which the version reaches the phone.

allowlist.justification: DECLARED harness deviation: the real bar is fixed against the viewport, which is correct in the app where the viewport is the phone. Inside an embedded phone frame it would pin to the window, so the prototype makes it absolute within the frame. The only accepted shell divergence.

outOfScope.$comment: Surfaces that exist in the app but are DELIBERATELY not covered by this prototype. Declared here so that « not measured » is a decision and never an oversight. Rule: never a half conversion — a surface speaks either the prototype's language (the .tm scope) or the old one, never both.
outOfScope./config: Out of scope by product decision. Not converted, not measured. A non-regression baseline must be frozen before conversion work begins.
outOfScope./systeme (interior): Receives health, runs and controls, but its mobile redesign is deferred. Only its reception is drawn; its internal template is not measured.
outOfScope./media/:provider/:id (implementation): The media sheet EXISTS and is conformant; the prototype draws its target but does not rebuild it. Measured for structure, not imposed pixel-wise on what already ships.
outOfScope.desktop >= md: The phone is the origin of the design; the large screen stays functional but is not specified to the pixel.

$reportedDefects.$comment: Defects found by hand on the running prototype, each covered by a test in harness/bugs.py — the project rule is that a bug gets its test, written together with the fix.
$reportedDefects.cron-cadence: The cadence displayed « 20 3,15 * * * » — raw jargon. Now translated, with an explicit fallback when the pattern is not recognised.
$reportedDefects.sheet-hidden-under-layer: « Voir la fiche » from a sheet opened the screen UNDER it (z-45 against z-47). The sheet now closes first.
$reportedDefects.navigation-does-not-close: Changing page left the media sheet open. Navigation now closes the layers.
$reportedDefects.carousel-blocks-scroll: `touch-action: pan-x` ALONE forbids vertical panning: a finger on the cast carousel froze the sheet. Both axes are allowed and the browser decides from the gesture direction.
$reportedDefects.action-glued-to-bar: A screen must reserve the height of the tab bar, which passes above it.
$reportedDefects.result-without-sheet: Search results offered no path to the media sheet. The poster is a button.
$reportedDefects.missing-way-out: The resolution screen PROMISED a pre-filled manual search without providing one. It exists, and turns the folder name into a query.
$reportedDefects.hollow-suggestion-sheet: A suggestion's sheet showed « Métadonnées inconnues / Genres inconnus »: the sheet table only carried library titles. Suggestions now carry real data, and only filled-in ones are served.
$reportedDefects.class-never-ported: The .nofiche class was used in markup without ever having been transplanted: the « no trailer » message rendered at 14px without its frame. CSS must be EXTRACTED, never rewritten from memory.
$reportedDefects.sheets-missing-for-follows: Followed films had no sheet: they live in acquire.db but NOT in library.db (not owned). Coverage is now systematic; the remaining gaps are unidentified release names, which have no sheet by definition.
$reportedDefects.poster-dead-link: A poster was a button even with no sheet behind it — a dead link is as bad as a greyed-out button. A poster is a button only when the sheet resolves.
$reportedDefects.identity-by-title: Sources disagree on titles (« Dexter Resurrection » vs « Dexter: Resurrection », truncated lists). The prototype resolves by normalised key; the APP must resolve by provider ID — identity by title is never identity.
$reportedDefects.add-button-inert: The media sheet's add button was left-aligned like an action row and never changed state. It is centred and toggles to outline + « Ajouté »/« Suivi », like a search result's button: one gesture, one answer, everywhere.
$reportedDefects.scroll-jumps-to-top: Ticking a box at the bottom of a form jumped back to the top: every toggle re-rendered the whole screen. Fixed in openScreen (position + focus + caret), with a restore AFTER images load, since the page is briefly too short.
$reportedDefects.inert-drawer: The hamburger opened nothing and the drawer links were not clickable: event delegation looked only at <button>, and a navigation link is an <a>.
$reportedDefects.inert-filters: The library's category pills were decorative: they changed state without filtering. They now carry each item's real category, combine with the search, and the sample guarantees no category is empty.
$reportedDefects.library-card-opens-acquisition-sheet: From the library, a card opened the ACQUISITION sheet — a second sheet design whose content also varied depending on whether the title was followed. A card's destination follows the page it lives on.
$reportedDefects.two-season-renderings: Media sheets rendered seasons either as a titled list or as a numbered matrix, and twelve sheets contained both at once. Episode titles and dates were fetched for every series so that one rendering serves them all.
$reportedDefects.episode-presence-guessed: Episode presence was derived from « number <= owned count », which assumes the hole sits at the end of the season. False for 35 series in this library. Presence is read from the list of owned numbers.
$reportedDefects.visual-on-one-sheet-in-six: Only media that already had a poster had received a wide visual, so one sheet in six opened on an image and the rest on a muted field. Every sheet now carries a visual at the same definition.

$adversarialReview.$comment: Every reported defect was generalised into a RULE checked across all states (harness/audit.py and audit2.py), not fixed on the reported case alone. The implementer inherits the rules, not the anecdotes.
$adversarialReview.R1: Every tappable poster leads to a FILLED-IN sheet (synopsis, genres, cast). Otherwise the poster is not a button.
$adversarialReview.R2: A button must have a declared DESTINATION, not merely a known class. A real href counts as a destination.
$adversarialReview.R3: Touch target >= 32px. DECLARED EXCEPTION: the episode cell is 31 × 27 in the shipped component — at 13 per row, 44px would demand 572px. A geometric constraint, not an oversight.
$adversarialReview.R4: No horizontal overflow outside declared scrollers (.pillscroll, .cast, .eps). An element clipped by an ancestor does not count, provided the clipping ancestor itself fits; the scrollport must also offer no real horizontal scrolling.
$adversarialReview.R5: A horizontal scroller NEVER sets touch-action: pan-x alone — it would block vertical panning.
$adversarialReview.R6: No essential title is truncated (.ht, .sheettitle, dialog title).
$adversarialReview.R7: No panel renders emptiness in silence.
$adversarialReview.R8: EVERY layer (screen, sheet) reserves the height of the tab bar that passes above it, AND its last VISIBLE button is reachable at maximum scroll.
$adversarialReview.R10: Every action mutates state, navigates, or opens a layer — never nothing.
$adversarialReview.R11: No visible jargon or technical value: undefined, NaN, null, [object, 0/0, cron expressions.
$adversarialReview.R12: ONE button system: height 44, radius 8, weight 600, 13.5px. Alignment — with an icon: left (the icon anchors the row); without: centred (nothing anchors the left edge).
$adversarialReview.R13: Identical section order across all media sheets; only nature-imposed sections vary. The sample is drawn from the data: complete, incomplete, without visual, film, series.
$adversarialReview.R14: Every layer closes via the scrim (sheets, dialogs) or via Back (screens).
$adversarialReview.R15: The three Suivis modes show the same number of items.
$adversarialReview.R16: The nav badge AND the tab badge equal to-grab + to-resolve, in both scenarios.
$adversarialReview.R17: Every destruction is confirmed (dialog) or reversible (undo), and never mutates before confirmation.
$adversarialReview.R18: Multiple selection works in BOTH library modes. It existed only on tiles: « Sélectionner » switched on in list mode with nothing selectable — a mode one can enter and do nothing in is worse than no mode.
$adversarialReview.R19: Nothing positions itself by a distance to a screen edge: the bar publishes its measured height into `--tm-bottom-bar-h` and everything sitting above it reads that.
$adversarialReview.R20: The library has ONE sub-line grammar: « year · type ». Films said « 2026 · Film » and series « 6 ép. » — two grammars make rows incomparable.
$adversarialReview.R21: An episode's state colour is SUBTLE: a 6px dot and the number in the tone. The title stays neutral — it is what one reads first. One colour signal per row.
$adversarialReview.R22: Every switch has exactly the same dimensions (46 × 28), whatever the neighbouring label's length. A « Oui/Non » chip in a flex row took the text's height.
$adversarialReview.R23: Within an option group, every row has the same size, and SHAPE states the rule: circle = single choice, square = multiple. Identical pills said nothing about how many could be picked.
$adversarialReview.R24: No form interaction moves the scroll position. Re-rendering the SAME screen preserves position, value and caret of the active field; a DIFFERENT screen starts at zero. The guard lives in one place.
$adversarialReview.R25: A filter FILTERS, and its parts sum to the whole: 717 + 528 + 382 + 73 + 66 + 56 + 31 + 8 = 1,861. A filter whose parts do not sum to the total is a filter that lies. Categories are the real storage ones.
$adversarialReview.R26: The melting visual header is a trait of ALL media sheets. Every sheet whose medium has a visual carries the header AND its legibility gradient, in BOTH themes, with the header in flow and the title overlapping its lower edge. A medium without a visual degrades to a short muted field — a declared difference, not an oversight.
$methodLessons: R12 accepted `justify-content: normal` as equivalent to « centred »: too slack, and it let through a misalignment that was later found by hand.
R8 covered screens only: the same defect came back through sheets. A rule must target the FAMILY, not the case.
A hardened R8 first accused a button inside a collapsed <details> — Chrome still gives it a layout box. A rule must judge what is VISIBLE, not DOM order.

R2 whitelisted by CLASS instead of requiring a destination. Three lenient rules in a row (« normal » for centred, screens without sheets, class for destination): a rule that is easy to satisfy proves nothing.

The hamburger and the drawer links escaped the audits: one whitelisted by its class, the others because detection looked only at <button>. An audit that inspects one element type has a blind spot the size of the other.

A screenshot fingerprint is NOT an oracle here: two captures of the SAME file diverge on 8 to 15 of the 45 states (skeleton shimmer, header entrance, async decode of embedded posters). Use bounding rects plus a computed-style subset; and for « is this rule dead? », the exact proof: querySelectorAll of the selector over all states, plus the fact that the code never writes the class.
« 0 violations across 0 rules » reads the same when all is well and when nothing runs. Both audit passes announce the rules EXECUTED and shout as soon as a declared rule stops running.

The export allowlist had drifted to 107 classes out of 237: more than half the CSS would never have reached the app. harness/export.py classifies every class by what it actually does and fails on anything uncovered or dead.
Slicing the stylesheet on the string « BLOCK 2 » cuts the header comment's opener and leaves an orphan closer: the header's own prose then parses as selectors. Slice from the comment opener.

Sampling a fixed handful of states hides whole families. R13 sampled five frozen states, none of them an incomplete medium — which is exactly where a divergence went unseen. Draw the sample from the DATA.
$adversarialReview.R27: A trailer ALWAYS opens in YouTube, never inside the application, and the sheet offers it wherever one arrives from. A real anchor, a conformant watch URL, target=_blank and noopener; no promise of in-app playback.
$adversarialReview.R28: Exactly ONE back-control design, compatible with every page, in the flow so it pushes content instead of covering it — and never text glued closer than 8px to it.
$adversarialReview.R29: Episode presence is read from the LIST of owned numbers, never from a « number <= owned count » threshold. Checked on every series with an internal hole, in both renderings.
$adversarialReview.R30: ONE season rendering, within a sheet and between sheets. The numbered matrix remains the declared fallback when a provider gives nothing.
$adversarialReview.R31: From the library, a card opens the media sheet, never the acquisition sheet.
$adversarialReview.R32: Découvrir offers three formats — list, posters, slide cards — and the gesture keeps ONE meaning across them. In the list and poster formats a swipe dismisses. In the slide cards, left « Passer » decides nothing and the card comes round again, right « Pas intéressé » removes it with an undo — the verbs are the ones the other formats already use, and no format invents an action of its own. A drag born on a card belongs to the card: without that claim the page-swipe handler fires too and navigates away mid-gesture.
$adversarialReview.R33: The slide-cards pile is ANIMATED, never rebuilt. Advancing moves the existing nodes — the outgoing card flies out, the ones behind change depth and their transition carries them forward, a new card is inserted at the back and rises from under the deck. Rebuilding the HTML replaces every node, and a replaced node cannot transition: the pile then cuts instead of moving. Checked mid-flight, not at rest: the same nodes must still be present, in motion, shortly after the gesture.
$adversarialReview.R34: A format that shows one poster full-screen carries its own source. The thumbnail poster is right at thumbnail size and mush once blown up; the slide cards use posters sized for the surface they fill. Only the served suggestions carry one, so the weight follows what is actually reachable.
